chunks: Al-Hakim Abu Ali Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Bayhaqi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sawli, saying: He narrated to us Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Nahwi, saying: He narrated to me Ibn Abi Abdoon from his father, saying:

When Al-Ma'mun pledged allegiance to Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) with the covenant, he seated him next to himself. Then Abbas the orator stood up, spoke, and spoke well, then concluded with reciting: 'People cannot do without a sun and a moon; you are the sun and he is that moon.'
ai.seo_question: What metaphor did Abbas use to describe the relationship between Al-Ma'mun and Imam Ar-Ridha?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* captures the political theater of Al-Ma'mun's appointment of Imam Ar-Ridha (a.s.), where Abbas ibn Abd al-Malik employed the celestial metaphor of the sun and moon to legitimize the Imam's elevated spiritual status alongside the Caliph's temporal authority. In Shia scholarly tradition, this distinction underscores the concept of *Wilayah* as a divine light that guides the community, even when embedded within the structures of political power. The metaphor reflects the complementary roles of governance and spiritual guidance, a theme central to understanding the Imamate's role during the Abbasid era.
